names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 14 mai, «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Terapont, Episcopul Ciprului».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Θεράπων επίσκοπος Κύπρου», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 25. мај ст. ст., „Свештеномученик Терапонт епископ кипарски“ — Свештеномученик is the `hieromartyr` this corpus puts in `types`, епископ the `bishop` it puts there and the `Bishop` in `office`, and „кипарски“ the see, which the display name already carries. Strip them and the bare personal name is what is left. **Measured, and the fold is the one to watch on this name**: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Терапонт», so this is the first folder to hold it — but **the Prologue prints the identical string for a different man on the Julian 27 May**, the bishop of Sardis, so a later reader working that day will fold onto this form and must keep `therapon-of-sardis` apart from `therapon-of-cyprus` by the see and not by the name. That is said here so the fold is a known one when it happens.

floruit.note: The page reasons rather than states, and says so: from his action against theopaschism and against iconoclasm «it reasons that he lived in the seventh century or the beginning of the eighth, but not later than 740, the year Andrew of Crete, the Jerusalemite, fell asleep», who praised him in an encomium late in his own life. The later bound is that argument's, not a recorded year.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 14 mai — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Terapont, Episcopul Ciprului»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Θεράπων επίσκοπος Κύπρου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: the bishop in Cyprus cut down on the holy table while he was serving. **He is not `therapon-of-sardis`**, which the namesweep flagged and which was read. **The page will not date him and this folder does not either.** It says outright that his birth year is entirely unknown and that his country is uncertain — some make him «ἐκ τῆς Ἑῴας», out of the East, as Andrew of Crete notes, and others «ἐκ τῆς τῶν Ἀλαμάνων χώρας», from the land of the Alamanni, that is from present-day Germany — and it reasons him to the seventh or the beginning of the eighth century only from his acts against theopaschism and iconoclasm, with an upper bound of 740, when Andrew of Crete, who wrote his encomium, died. That is the page's inference and not a date it states, so no `dates` object is added and the reasoning is recorded here. **The see is given as Kition** — «έγινε επίσκοπος Κιτίου στην Κύπρο» — where the existing folder's `office` is the bare word Bishop. **It adds the relics and the myrrh**: the relic taken to Constantinople, first to the church of the Mother of God at Blachernae and then to a church of his own name, where a small shrine inside the walls still streams myrrh; and portions at Zographou on the Holy Mountain, at his church in Zografou of Athens and at his church in Mytilene. He is named patron of Zografou. **One apolytikion, in Ἦχος α´, naming him** — «τρυφᾶς Θεράπων μάρτυς» — is copied whole; it is not a mis-hang, and it is the service Nikodemos the Hagiorite wrote for him, corrected in 1785 by the archdeacon Agapios of Paros.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.06.2026 (25. мај ст. ст.) — „Свештеномученик Терапонт епископ кипарски“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23, 24 and 25 May is. **A DAY NEITHER OTHER CALENDAR KEEPS HIM ON**: doxologia and saint.gr both keep him on 14 May and this book on 25 May, so the row is written on the 25/5 and the other two rows are left where they are. The day list for the menologion 25/5 could not see him for that reason, and `sr-namesweep.mjs` found him because the heading carries his see. **AND THE PROLOGUE ITSELF PROVES THERE ARE TWO THERAPONS.** Two days later, on the Julian 27 May, it prints „Свештеномученик Терапонт, епископ сардијски“ — the same rank, a different see. The corpus keeps both, `therapon-of-cyprus` and `therapon-of-sardis`, and **two commemorations on one calendar means two men**, so this row belongs to the Cypriot alone and the 27 May is a different folder’s business. **`ascetic` ADDED; `wonderworker` REFUSED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHO THE WORD IS SAID OF.** „Монах и подвижник на острву Кипру“ — Подвижник is a noun said of the man and maps to `ascetic` in BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5, and `ascetic` is **not in `src/lib/honorific.js`’s `PRECEDENCE`**, so the page goes on reading *Hieromartyr Therapon* and the word shows only in the facts line. **Чудотворац is never said of him**: what the entry calls чудотворне are his **relics** — „мошти ове чудотворне“ — and the object of a wonder is not its subject, so `wonderworker` is not added. `hieromartyr`, `bishop` and `monk` are all three corroborated: „Свештеномученик“, „епископ кипарски“, „Монах“. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE ONE YEAR HERE HAS NO FIELD TO HOLD IT.** The folder holds `floruit` 601 to 740, `inferred`, which saint.gr reasons from Andrew of Crete’s death. **The Prologue gives 806** — „у време цара Никифора године 806, ударише Агарјани на острво Кипар“ — **but that is the year his relics were moved, not a year of his life**, and there is no field for a translation of relics. It is the sixth such year in this wave and it stands in the prose. **It does not contradict the floruit**: a man who died not later than 740 can have his relics carried off in 806, and the two readings sit together. The reign of Nicephorus is used for nothing. **New here, and most of the entry is new.** doxologia already had the Agarenes taking counsel against Cyprus and the saint ordering his own translation by a revelation; this book says **to whom** he appeared — **the warden of the church where his body lay** — and what followed: that **when the ship with the reliquary put to sea a great storm rose, while around the ship the sea was calm**; that **a sweet fragrance poured out of the reliquary over the whole ship and all about it**; that **the warden opened it and all saw it filled with myrrh flowing from the relics**, with which **many sick were anointed and made well**; that **a church was built over these wonderworking relics at Constantinople**; and that by the grace of God the gravest sick were healed at them **of palsy, of cancer, of haemorrhage, of madness, of blindness, of withering, and of various other torments**. saint.gr has the myrrh-streaming shrine inside the walls; this is the myrrh at sea that began it. **The emperor Nicephorus and the church warden gain nothing** by the coordinator’s third ruling: no calendar read for this corpus keeps either, and the warden is not even named. `related` untouched at `andrew-of-crete`, whom this entry does not name. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Ἀσκήσει μὲν τὸ πρῶτον λάμψας Ὅσιε, πάσας δαιμόνων φάλαγγας κατετρόπωσας, ἀθλήσει δὲ τὸ δεύτερον ἀριστεύσας τὰς τῶν τυράννων ἀπειλὰς κατεφρόνησας. Διὸ διπλοῦν παρὰ Θεοῦ στέφος λαβών, συγχαίρεις τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῖς χοροῖς, καὶ τρυφᾶς Θεράπων μάρτυς, σὺν τοῖς ὁσίοις καὶ ἱερομάρτυσι. Δόξα τῷ σὲ δοξάσαντι Χριστῷ, Δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι, Δόξα τῷ ἐνεργοῦντι διὰ σοῦ πᾶσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α´, on the page of Άγιος Θεράπων επίσκοπος Κύπρου

english.text: Shining first in ascetic labour, venerable father, you routed all the phalanxes of the demons; and excelling secondly in the martyr's contest, you despised the threats of the tyrants. And so, having received a double crown from God, you rejoice with the choirs of the angels and delight, Therapon the martyr, together with the venerable and the hieromartyrs. Glory to Christ who glorified you, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.
